# Kubernetes agent tools

The `k8s` agent (`k8s_agent`) publishes 16 tools to the [Tool Registry](../TOOL_REGISTRY.md). This page is generated from the agent's code: names, descriptions and parameters come from the tool definitions, action classes from `audit.ToolClassification`, and capabilities and eligibility from the agent card options. Capability names are defined in the [capability vocabulary](capabilities.md).

| [`describe_pod`](#describe_pod) | read | `pod_detail` |

| [`get_endpoints`](#get_endpoints) | read | `service_info` |

| [`get_pod_logs`](#get_pod_logs) | read | `logs` |
| [`get_pod_resources`](#get_pod_resources) | read | `resource_usage` |
| [`get_pods`](#get_pods) | read | `pod_list` |
| [`get_service`](#get_service) | read | `service_info` |
| [`patch_deployment_resources`](#patch_deployment_resources) | destructive | `resource_limits_change`, `workload_restart` |

## `debug_node_dmesg`

Pull the kernel ring buffer (dmesg) from a Kubernetes worker node via a short-lived debug pod. Use when node-level pressure (MemoryPressure, DiskPressure from get_node_status, or node warnings from get_events) can't be explained by pod/container-level tools. Node name comes from a prior get_pods or describe_pod call.

- **Action class:** write
- **Capabilities:** `kernel_log`, `debug_pod_create`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.10 `debug_node_dmesg` — worker-node kernel log pull](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#110-debug_node_dmesg--worker-node-kernel-log-pull)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `node_name` | string | yes | The exact node name to pull dmesg from. Use get_nodes, get_node_status, or the 'node' field returned by get_pods/describe_pod to find it. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `lines` | integer | no | Number of most recent dmesg lines to return (default 200, max 2000). |

## `delete_pod`

Delete a Kubernetes pod by name. The deployment controller will reschedule it. Use to restart a stuck or crash-looping pod without affecting other replicas.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `workload_restart`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.7 `delete_pod` — single pod deletion](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#17-delete_pod--single-pod-deletion)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace of the pod. |
| `pod_name` | string | yes | The exact pod name to delete. Use get_pods to find the name. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `grace_period_seconds` | integer | no | Seconds for graceful termination (default: pod's terminationGracePeriodSeconds). Use 0 for immediate deletion. |

## `describe_pod`

Get detailed information about a Kubernetes pod including status, conditions, events, and container details.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `pod_detail`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.6 `describe_pod` — read-only inspector](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#16-describe_pod--read-only-inspector)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pod_name` | string | yes | The exact pod name to describe. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `namespace` | string | no | The Kubernetes namespace of the pod (e.g., 'default', 'kube-system'). |

## `get_endpoints`

List Kubernetes endpoints to verify which pod IPs are registered as backends for a service. Empty endpoints indicate selector mismatch or no ready pods.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `service_info`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Check if the database service has healthy endpoints"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace to check endpoints in. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `endpoint_name` | string | no | Optional specific endpoint name (usually matches service name). |

## `get_events`

List Kubernetes events sorted by time. Useful for finding warnings, errors, and recent changes that might explain issues.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `event_list`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Show recent warning events in the cluster"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace to get events from. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `event_type` | string | no | Optional filter by event type: Normal or Warning. |
| `resource_name` | string | no | Optional filter events related to a specific resource name. |

## `get_node_status`

Show node health conditions (MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure, Ready) and allocatable vs capacity CPU/memory. Use to diagnose scheduling failures or resource exhaustion.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `node_health`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `node_name` | string | no | Specific node name. If empty, returns status for all nodes. |

## `get_nodes`

List Kubernetes cluster nodes showing status, roles, age, version, and resource capacity.

- **Action class:** read

- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `show_labels` | boolean | no | If true, show node labels in output. |

## `get_pod_logs`

Retrieve logs from a Kubernetes pod. Can get logs from specific containers and previous crashed instances.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "Get the last 100 lines of logs from the postgres pod"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pod_name` | string | yes | The exact pod name to get logs from (e.g., 'nginx-7d6877d777-abc12'). |
| `container` | string | no | Container name, only needed if pod has multiple containers. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `namespace` | string | no | The Kubernetes namespace of the pod (e.g., 'default', 'kube-system'). |
| `previous` | boolean | no | If true, get logs from the previous container instance (useful for crash loops). |
| `tail_lines` | integer | no | Number of recent log lines to retrieve (default 50). |

## `get_pod_resources`

Show CPU and memory requests, limits, and live usage (from metrics-server) for containers in a namespace. Use to identify over- or under-provisioned workloads.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `resource_usage`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace to query. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `pod_name` | string | no | Specific pod name. If empty, returns resources for all pods in the namespace. |

## `get_pods`

List Kubernetes pods in a namespace with optional label filtering. Shows pod status, restarts, age, and node placement.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `pod_list`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **Example prompts:** "List all pods in the database namespace"

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace to list pods from. Use 'all' for all namespaces. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `labels` | string | no | Optional label selector to filter pods (e.g., 'app=postgres'). |

## `get_service`

|---|---|---|---|
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace to list services from. |

## `patch_deployment_resources`

Patch a deployment's container memory limit and request (e.g. to fix an undersized limit causing OOMKilled). Triggers a rollout restart of the pod. Use get_pod_resources first to determine the current limit before calculating a new one.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `resource_limits_change`, `workload_restart`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deployment` | string | yes | The name of the deployment to patch. Use get_pods or kubectl get deployments to find the name. |
| `memory_limit` | string | yes | New memory limit (e.g. '1Gi' or '512Mi'). Use get_pod_resources first to determine the current limit and calculate the new one. |
| `memory_request` | string | yes | New memory request (e.g. '768Mi'). Should not exceed memory_limit. |
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace of the deployment. |
| `container` | string | no | Specific container name to patch. If empty, applies to all containers in the pod template (kubectl's default). |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |

## `read_pod_file`

Read a file directly from inside a running pod via kubectl exec. Use when PostgreSQL logs to a file (logging_collector=on) rather than stdout, making get_pod_logs return empty. Supports optional line-count limit and keyword filter.

- **Action class:** read
- **Capabilities:** `logs`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file_path` | string | yes | Absolute path of the file to read inside the container (e.g. '/var/lib/postgresql/data/log/postgresql.log'). |
| `pod_name` | string | yes | The exact pod name to read a file from. |
| `container` | string | no | Container name, only needed if pod has multiple containers. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
| `filter` | string | no | Optional string to filter lines (case-insensitive grep). Use to focus on FATAL, PANIC, or other keywords. |
| `namespace` | string | no | The Kubernetes namespace of the pod. |
| `tail_lines` | integer | no | Return only the last N lines of the file (default: all lines). |

## `restart_deployment`

Perform a rolling restart of all pods in a deployment (kubectl rollout restart). Replaces pods one at a time to avoid downtime. Use when all replicas are unhealthy or after a config change.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `workload_restart`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.8 `restart_deployment` — rolling restart](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#18-restart_deployment--rolling-restart)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deployment` | string | yes | The name of the deployment to restart. Use get_pods or kubectl get deployments to find the name. |
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace of the deployment. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |

## `scale_deployment`

Scale a deployment to the specified number of replicas. Can scale up to add capacity or scale down (including to 0) to stop workloads. Use with caution — scaling to 0 causes downtime.

- **Action class:** destructive
- **Capabilities:** `deployment_scale`
- **Fleet eligible:** no
- **Auto-remediation eligible:** no
- **See also:**
  - [MUTATION_TOOLS.md › 1.9 `scale_deployment` — replica count change](../MUTATION_TOOLS.md#19-scale_deployment--replica-count-change)
  - [ROLLBACK.md › 3.1 Kubernetes](../ROLLBACK.md#31-kubernetes)

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deployment` | string | yes | The name of the deployment to scale. |
| `namespace` | string | yes | The Kubernetes namespace of the deployment. |
| `replicas` | integer | yes | Target replica count. Use 0 to scale down completely. |
| `context` | string | no | Kubernetes context to use. If empty, uses current context. |
